decision.text: D10: The builder writes a new file cairn/tools/base/proofs/suite_parity.py (it does not exist yet). `python3 cairn/tools/base/proofs/suite_parity.py --baseline <out.json>` runs `bin/cairn test -q`, collects the red proof paths it prints, and writes {"measured_at", "command", "red": [<repo-relative proof paths>]} to <out.json> through the artifact door; `python3 cairn/tools/base/proofs/suite_parity.py <baseline.json>` runs the same command and exits 0 only when every red it sees is in the baseline's "red" list, printing each new red. Before any of D2-D8 lands, the builder runs it once with --baseline CairnCommons/measurements/2026-10-29-suite-reds-before-the-ticket-split.json (a new file).

suite_parity.py already stands at cairn/tools/base/proofs/suite_parity.py, committed with the red-first proof (2162ff41) and written to exactly the contract D10 states; the builder does not write it again, it only runs --baseline before D2-D8 land and the comparison after.

D11: The migration is one act, run after D2-D8 and D12 have landed and D9's fixture teeth are green. The charter's plan_fields is narrowed to exactly the census summary.plan (14 names) through the artifact door; then ticket_log.split runs over every ticket_file.plans(CairnCommons/tickets) path with actor 'cc' and why naming this ticket; then for every ticket reconstruct(plan, log lines the split added, state) is compared with the plan as it stood at HEAD (git show HEAD:<path>), and the run stops at the first mismatch, naming it. All of it, charter included, is one CairnCommons commit. A ticket the split cannot move is named and the commit is not made.
